q: Feyenoord's heaviest ever defeat came at PSV in October 2010. What was the score?
sub: Jonathan Reis scored a hat-trick. Feyenoord coach Mario Been kept his job.
note: Facts confirmed (24 Oct 2010, 10-0, Reis hat-trick, Been kept his job). Dropped as a straight mirror of a shipping question: 'Which club lost 10-0 away to PSV in October 2010, the heaviest defeat in its history?'

q: Nine months after the 10-0, Feyenoord's players held a vote on coach Mario Been. What was the outcome?
a: Thirteen of eighteen had no confidence in him, and he left in July 2011
sub: Captain Ron Vlaar called the meeting. Van Geel said Been felt betrayed.
note: Vote confirmed: 13 of 18 against, the other five abstained, Been left on 13 July 2011. Sub corrected: it was technical director Martin van Geel who said Been felt betrayed. Been himself only said he was deeply affected.

q: Which PSV left-back was sent off after 29 seconds at NAC in February 2015, the fastest Eredivisie red card from kick-off?
sub: He never touched Gill Swerts. The KNVB later dropped the case.
note: Confirmed: 3 February 2015 at NAC, 29 seconds, the fastest from kick-off in the Eredivisie, beating Kalou's 61 seconds. He never touched Swerts and the KNVB dropped the case, so no suspension followed.

q: Philips came off the front of PSV's shirt in 2016 after 34 years. Which energy brand replaced it?
sub: A three-year deal worth 18 million euros.
note: Confirmed: announced on 21 April 2016, on the shirt from 2016-17, after 34 years of Philips on the front. At least 18 million euros over three years. Philips stayed on as sleeve sponsor.

q: In May 2016 the KNVB ordered which club relegated for hiding parts of its deal with the investment fund Doyen?
sub: An appeal saved them. They got a 181,000 euro fine and a three-year European ban instead.
note: Dropped as a mirror of a shipping BALL row: 'In May 2016 the KNVB licensing committee ordered which club relegated for financial mismanagement, a decision overturned on appeal?' The sub was also embroidered: the three-year European ban came from the licensing committee in December 2015, not from the June 2016 appeal.

q: FC Twente, champions in 2010, finished bottom in 2018. Their relegation was sealed by a 5-0 defeat at which club?
sub: Five wins all season. Gertjan Verbeek was sacked and Marino Pusic could not save them.
note: Confirmed: the 5-0 at Vitesse on 29 April 2018 ended 34 unbroken years in the top flight, five wins all season, Verbeek sacked, Pusic could not save them.

q: A week after losing the 2011 cup final to Twente, Ajax hosted them in a title decider needing a win. What was the score?
sub: Siem de Jong twice and a Landzaat own goal. Ajax's 30th title and a third star.
note: Confirmed: 15 May 2011, a week after the cup final, 3-1, Siem de Jong twice and a Landzaat own goal, Ajax's 30th title and the third star.

q: Ajax led the 2011 cup final against FC Twente 2-0. How did it end?
sub: Marc Janko headed the winner from a Theo Janssen free kick.
note: Confirmed (Ajax 2-0 up through De Zeeuw and Ebecilio, Twente 3-2 in extra time, Janko on 117). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping row 'Which club did FC Twente beat 3-2 after extra time in the 2011 KNVB Cup final?'. The sub's 'free kick' was also unsupported: sources say only that Janssen supplied the ball.

q: FC Twente's ground was called the Arke Stadion until 2008, after a travel company. Which brewer took over the name?
note: Confirmed: Arke was a Dutch travel firm, Grolsch took the naming rights in 2008 and the ground became De Grolsch Veste.

q: Which English manager gave a 2008 television interview in English with a thick Dutch accent, shortly after arriving at FC Twente?
sub: The clip has followed him around ever since, right up to the Jamaica job in 2024.
note: Interview confirmed, McClaren appointed at Twente on 20 June 2008. Sub reworded: 'resurfaced every time he got a new job' cannot be verified as literally true, so it now names a documented resurfacing.

q: Martin Jol's Ajax scored 106 goals and took 85 points in 2009-10. Where did they finish?
sub: Suárez scored 35 of them. Ajax did win the cup.
note: Confirmed (106 goals, 85 points, second, one behind Twente). Dropped because a shipping question states the answer in its own text: 'Who was Ajax's head coach in 2009-10, when they finished a point behind Twente?'

q: AZ became champions in April 2009 on a Sunday when they did not play. Which club's 6-2 defeat at PSV settled it?
sub: AZ had lost at Vitesse the day before.
note: Mirror of the shipping row 'Ajax lost 6-2 away to which club on 19 April 2009, the result that made AZ champions that afternoon?'. The sub was also wrong: AZ lost 2-1 to Vitesse at home in Alkmaar, not away.

q: In March 2008 Louis van Gaal announced he would leave AZ that summer. Why did he end up staying?
a: The players asked him to stay
sub: A year later he won them the title.
note: Confirmed: announced on 28 March 2008 that he would leave, stayed at the squad's request, title a year later. The old src, the English Wikipedia AZ season page, supports none of it, so it is swapped for a contemporary report.

q: AZ lost their first two league games of 2008-09, to NAC and at ADO. What happened next?
a: A 28-match unbeaten run and the title
note: Confirmed: beaten 2-1 at home by NAC on 31 August 2008 and 3-0 at ADO on 13 September, then 28 league games unbeaten and the title with 80 points.

q: Six months after AZ's 2009 title, owner Dirk Scheringa's bank collapsed. Name the bank.
sub: Bankrupt on 19 October 2009. He resigned as AZ chairman ten days later.
note: Confirmed (DSB Bank, bankrupt 19 Oct 2009, Scheringa resigned ten days later). Dropped because DSB Bank is already the answer to a shipping row about the AZ stadium name.

q: In November 2011 the Ajax supervisory board appointed which man as director general at a meeting Johan Cruyff was barely told about?
sub: A judge suspended it in December 2011 and the appeal court upheld that ban in February 2012.
note: Appointment confirmed (16 November 2011, Cruyff told only that afternoon). Sub was invented: no court annulled it. A preliminary relief judge suspended it on 12 December 2011 and the Amsterdam appeal court upheld the ban on 7 February 2012.

q: Feyenoord could have clinched the 2017 title at Excelsior on 7 May. What happened?
sub: Fans rioted on the Coolsingel. A week later Kuyt's hat-trick beat Heracles.
note: Confirmed (7 May 2017, 3-0, Coolsingel riots, Kuyt hat-trick a week later). Dropped as a mirror of 'Feyenoord lost 3-0 to which Rotterdam neighbour on 7 May 2017, missing their first chance to clinch the title?'

q: How many days after his title-winning hat-trick in May 2017 did Dirk Kuyt announce his retirement?
sub: Hat-trick on Sunday 14 May, retirement on Wednesday 17 May, aged 36.
note: Confirmed (hat-trick Sunday 14 May, retirement Wednesday 17 May, aged 36). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping row 'Which Feyenoord captain announced his retirement three days after the 2017 title?'

q: Feyenoord fans damaged which 17th-century fountain in Rome before a Europa League game in February 2015?
a: The Barcaccia, at the foot of the Spanish Steps
sub: Six fans were later convicted in their absence.
note: Confirmed: 19 February 2015, the Barcaccia at the foot of the Spanish Steps, Bernini, 1620s. Six fans were convicted in absentia by a Rome court in January 2021.

q: On the last day of 2015-16 Ajax needed a win at relegated De Graafschap to be champions. What happened?
a: They drew 1-1 and PSV took the title
sub: PSV won 3-1 at PEC Zwolle to finish two points clear.
note: Dropped as a mirror of 'Ajax drew 1-1 away at which club on the final day of 2015-16, handing the title to PSV?'. The word 'relegated' was also wrong on the day: De Graafschap finished 17th on 8 May and only went down on 22 May, after the play-offs.

q: PSV clinched the 2018 title by beating their only remaining rival 3-0 in April. Which club?
sub: Ajax had two men sent off late on and did not form a guard of honour.
note: Confirmed (15 April 2018, 3-0, two late Ajax red cards, no guard of honour). Dropped as a mirror of 'PSV clinched the 2017-18 title on 15 April 2018 with a 3-0 home win over which rival?'

q: The 2010 cup final between Ajax and Feyenoord was played over two legs. Why?
a: Safety and police costs, so neither leg had away fans
sub: Ajax won 2-0 at home and 4-1 in De Kuip.
note: Confirmed: played over two legs on safety grounds and because of policing costs, with no away fans at either leg. Ajax won 2-0 at home and 4-1 in De Kuip.

q: Three months after beating Ajax 5-1 in the 2014 cup final, PEC Zwolle beat them again for the Johan Cruijff Schaal. What was the score?
sub: Stefan Nijland, in the Amsterdam Arena.
note: Dropped as a mirror of 'Which club won the 2014 Johan Cruijff Schaal, beating Ajax 1-0 as cup holders?'. The interval was also wrong: cup final 20 April 2014, Schaal 3 August 2014, so three and a half months.

q: Heerenveen's first major trophy came in the 2009 cup final, on penalties. Which club did they beat?
sub: 2-2 after extra time. Gerald Sibon scored the decisive kick.
note: Confirmed (2-2, Sibon's decisive kick). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping EASY row 'Which Frisian club won the 2009 KNVB Cup, beating FC Twente on penalties after a 2-2 draw?'

q: Which club reached its first ever KNVB Cup final in 2012 and lost 3-0 to PSV?
note: Confirmed (8 April 2012, 3-0). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping row 'Which club won the 2012 KNVB Cup final 3-0 against Heracles Almelo?'

q: Feyenoord marked their centenary season in 2008 by winning the cup. Which Limburg club did they beat 2-0 in the final?
note: Confirmed: 27 April 2008, 2-0 against Roda JC, in the season Feyenoord marked 100 years.

q: FC Groningen's first ever major trophy came in the 2015 cup final. Which club did they beat 2-0?
sub: Both goals by the Slovak Albert Rusnák.
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a near-verbatim duplicate of a shipping row: 'Which club did FC Groningen beat 2-0 in the 2015 KNVB Cup final?', with the same answer.

q: Vitesse won their first major trophy in 125 years in the 2017 cup final. Who scored both goals against AZ?
sub: Both in the last ten minutes.
note: Confirmed (both goals, 81 and 88 minutes). Dropped as a mirror of 'Ricky van Wolfswinkel scored both goals in the 2017 KNVB Cup final. Which club was he playing for?'

q: Which Chelsea loanee was voted Vitesse's player of the year in 2017-18 as a teenager?
sub: Fourteen goals and ten assists in 39 games.
note: Confirmed: Vitesse player of the year 2017-18 on loan from Chelsea, aged 18 turning 19, 14 goals and 10 assists in 39 games. The src actually covers the provincial award rather than the club one, but the claim holds elsewhere.

q: Which future Manchester United midfielder spent 2010-11 on loan at Vitesse from Chelsea?
note: Loan confirmed (23 August 2010, 28 games). Reworded: he was already a Chelsea player, so 'future Chelsea midfielder' read wrong.

q: In August 2010 Vitesse became the first Dutch professional club in foreign hands. Which country was the buyer from?
sub: He promised the title within three years, then sold to a Russian in 2013.
note: Confirmed: 16 August 2010, the first Dutch professional club to pass into foreign hands, Merab Jordania of Georgia, who promised the title within three years and sold to a Russian owner in October 2013.

q: Which bird flew a lap of the GelreDome before every Vitesse home game from January 2010?
sub: He lands on his handler's glove for a turkey leg.
note: Confirmed: first flight on 31 January 2010 against PSV, a lap of the GelreDome before home games, and the turkey leg is in the source in as many words.

q: Which former Nigeria coach did Fortuna Sittard suspend in February 2018, months before they won promotion?
sub: He said he refused to join illegal activities. The club said he bullied staff.
note: Suspension confirmed (14 February 2018), promotion clinched on 28 April 2018, so 'three months' was two and a half. Softened to 'months'. Worth knowing: an arbitration commission later found no reprehensible conduct on his part.

q: Fortuna Sittard were bought in 2016 by a former Galatasaray official from which country?
sub: 85 percent of the club for a reported 870,000 euros.
note: Confirmed (21 July 2016, 85 percent, a reported 870,000 euros, former Galatasaray chief operating officer). The club-site src is now a 404, so it is swapped.

q: Roda JC's new investor Aleksei Korotaev was arrested in February 2017, a week after arriving at the club. Where?
a: Dubai airport, over a bounced cheque
sub: 17.7 million euros. He was cleared years later, the signature had been forged.
note: Confirmed: presented at Kerkrade on 3 February 2017 and arrested in Dubai days later over a bounced cheque for 17.7 million euros. Acquitted in 2021, the judge finding the signature forged.

q: In 2010 MVV were saved from bankruptcy when the city of Maastricht bought which asset for 1.85 million euros?
sub: The city also wrote off a debt of well over a million euros.
note: Purchase confirmed at 1.85 million euros. The write-off figure is not settled: the NOS src says 1.7 million, PropertyNL says 1.4 million, so the sub now avoids the disputed number.

q: Which Eredivisie club spent 2016 in court against its own Chinese owner over millions in promised money?
sub: Wang Hui of United Vansen was suspended as chairman of the supervisory board.
note: Confirmed: the Ondernemingskamer case ran through 2016 over just over 2 million euros in promised money, and Wang Hui was suspended as chairman of the supervisory board on 19 December 2016.

q: FC Emmen reached the Eredivisie for the first time in 2018 by winning 3-1 away at which club in the play-off final?
sub: Sparta went down. Drenthe had its first top-flight club.
note: Confirmed (20 May 2018, Sparta 1-3 Emmen, 3-1 on aggregate). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping row 'Which club won promotion to the Eredivisie in 2018 for the first time in its history, beating Sparta in the play-off final?'

q: In May 2010 Sparta were relegated in a play-off final against their Rotterdam neighbours. Which club went up in their place?
sub: 0-0 at Woudestein, 1-1 at Het Kasteel. Sparta spent six years in the second tier.
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a duplicate of the shipping row 'Sparta went down in 2010 after a play-off final against which Rotterdam rival, decided on away goals after 0-0 and 1-1?', same answer.

q: Go Ahead Eagles ended seventeen years outside the top flight in 2013. Which club did they beat in the play-off final?
sub: 3-0 at home, then a 1-0 defeat in Volendam. Their coach was Erik ten Hag.
note: Promotion confirmed, seventeen years confirmed, Ten Hag confirmed. Sub was misleading: '3-0 and 1-0' read as two wins. Go Ahead won 3-0 at home on 23 May and lost the return 1-0 on 26 May, 3-1 on aggregate.

q: Go Ahead Eagles lost the 2015 relegation play-off to De Graafschap. Who did they beat to go straight back up in 2016?
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a duplicate of the shipping row 'Which club went down in 2016 after losing the play-off final to Go Ahead Eagles?', same answer.

q: Willem II stayed up in 2010 by beating which club 3-0 after extra time in the play-off final?
sub: Go Ahead had won the first leg in Deventer with a last-minute goal.
note: Confirmed (16 May 2010, 3-0 after extra time). Dropped as an exact mirror of 'Which club stayed up in 2010 by beating Go Ahead Eagles 3-0 after extra time in the second leg of the play-off final?'

q: Roda JC dropped out of the Eredivisie in 2018 after losing a play-off at home to which second-tier club?
note: Confirmed (1-2 at home, 13 May 2018). Dropped as a mirror of 'Which club went down in 2018 after losing both legs of a play-off tie to Almere City?'

q: NEC went down in 2017 after losing a play-off to which club, who came straight back up?
note: Dropped as a mirror of 'Which club went down in 2017 after losing the play-off final 5-1 on aggregate to NAC Breda?'. 'Came straight back up' was also false: NAC had spent two seasons in the Eerste Divisie.

q: Which club dropped out of the Eredivisie in 2014 after losing a play-off to Excelsior?
note: Confirmed (Excelsior 4-2 on aggregate). Dropped as a mirror of 'Which club beat RKC Waalwijk in the 2014 play-off final to go up?'

q: Willem II kept their Eredivisie place in 2016 by beating which Brabant rival in the play-offs?
note: Confirmed (4-3 on aggregate). Dropped as a mirror of 'Which club stayed up in 2016 by beating NAC Breda in the play-off final?'

q: Which club sat bottom of the Eredivisie from the first weekend of 2010-11 to the last, finishing with fifteen points?
sub: Three wins all season.
note: Confirmed (18th, 15 points, three wins, bottom from first weekend to last). Dropped as a duplicate of 'Which club finished bottom in 2010-11 with 15 points and a goal difference of minus 61?'

q: Which club went up in 2007, down in 2008, up in 2009, down in 2013 and up again in 2017?
note: Confirmed on all five moves: promoted 2007, relegated 2008, Eerste Divisie champions 2009, relegated 2013, champions again 2017.

q: Which Japanese defender at VVV-Venlo scored a bicycle kick in September 2011 that was named Eredivisie goal of the season?
sub: Southampton signed him a year later.
note: Confirmed: 11 September 2011 against PSV in a 3-3 draw, voted Eredivisie goal of the season, and Southampton signed him at the end of August 2012.

q: Besides Ajax, PSV and Feyenoord, which club had never been relegated from the Eredivisie by the end of 2017-18?
note: Confirmed: at the end of 2017-18, Utrecht was the only club outside the big three never relegated from the Eredivisie. FC Twente, the other name people reach for, went down that very season.

q: Which top Dutch referee ran a Jumbo supermarket in Oldenzaal while taking charge of Eredivisie games?
sub: It was voted the best Jumbo in the country.
note: Confirmed: Kuipers ran the Jumbo in Oldenzaal while refereeing at the top, and it was voted the best Jumbo in the country in December 2016.

q: PSV's mascot Phoxy is a fox wearing number 99. The odd Ph in his name is a nod to which former main sponsor?
note: Confirmed. Reworded: the Ph is a nod to Philips, not an abbreviation, so 'what do the letters stand for' overstated it.

q: Ajax's mascot Lucky, on duty since 2000, is what kind of animal?
sub: Replaced by his son Lucky Junior in December 2015.
note: Confirmed: Lucky is a lynx, on duty from 2000, replaced by Lucky Junior on 20 December 2015.

q: Feyenoord's mascot Coentje is named after which club legend?
note: Confirmed: Feyenoord's mascot Coentje is named after Coen Moulijn.

q: FC Twente's loudest supporters stand in a section known by a single letter. Which letter?
note: Confirmed: Vak-P, the FC Twente supporters' section and association founded on 18 February 1991, named after a terrace in the old Diekman.

q: What two-word phrase do Dutch fans use for a floodlit night game in Breda?
note: Confirmed: avondje NAC, from the club's move to evening kick-offs in the 1970s.

q: Zwolle's club played as FC Zwolle from 1990 until 2012, when it went back to which name?
note: Confirmed: bankrupt in March 1990 and relaunched as FC Zwolle, renamed PEC Zwolle on 14 April 2012 after promotion.

q: Deventer fans call Go Ahead Eagles 'Kowet'. Where does that come from?
a: A local mangling of the English words Go Ahead
note: Confirmed: Kowet is how Go Ahead comes out in Deventer dialect. The club-site src returns 403, so it is swapped for a reachable one.

q: SC Cambuur's badge carries which animal, taken from the coat of arms of the Cammingha family?
sub: Cambuur is a contraction of Camminghaburen, the Leeuwarden neighbourhood named after the family.
note: Badge confirmed: a reclining red stag from the Van Cammingha arms, permission given in 1964. Sub corrected: the family named the neighbourhood Camminghaburen, and Cambuur is a contraction of that, so the castle was one step too far along the chain.

q: Heerenveen's shirt copies which flag, complete with its red water-lily leaves?
note: Confirmed: blue and white stripes with seven red water-lily leaves from the Frisian flag, in use since 1933.

q: Which anthem is sung before every Heerenveen home game?
sub: A tradition since 1990, played by a Frisian brass band.
note: Confirmed: the Frisian anthem has been played before every Eredivisie and cup match at Heerenveen since 1990. Moved out of ball: charming, but the answer draws no gasp. Sub added.

q: Which club is nicknamed Het Andere Oranje, the other orange, because of its shirt?
note: Confirmed: orange shirt, black shorts, nickname Het Andere Oranje, used by the club itself for its business club. Moved to normal: the answer is a plain fact with no story.

q: In August 2013 NEC sacked Alex Pastoor after how many league games of the new season?
sub: At the time the quickest sacking in Eredivisie history.
note: Confirmed: sacked after three league games in August 2013 following 1-4, 0-5 and 1-5, and it was the quickest in Eredivisie history at the time. Correctly hedged as 'at the time', since a later coach was also sacked after three rounds.

q: Alex Pastoor, sacked by NEC after three games in 2013, won promotion as champions in 2016 with which club?
note: Confirmed: Sparta won the 2015-16 Eerste Divisie under Pastoor, sealed on 11 April with a 3-1 win over Jong Ajax. Moved to extreme: an anorak follow-up with no story of its own.

q: Which Netherlands manager left the national team after Euro 2008 to take over Ajax, and quit after a single season?
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a mirror of the shipping EASY row 'Which Dutch legend, a three-time Ballon d'Or winner, coached Ajax in 2008-09 and resigned at the end of the season?'

q: How many matches did the KNVB ban Luis Suárez for after he bit Otman Bakkal in November 2010?
sub: Ajax had already suspended him for two.
note: Confirmed: seven-match KNVB ban on 24 November 2010, Ajax had already given him two. Moved to extreme: the answer is a bare number, and the bite itself is already a shipping BALL question in the Classic bank.

q: Which Brabant club, in the Eredivisie as recently as 2006, was declared bankrupt in June 2011?
sub: A debt of 5.2 million euros. The town refused to guarantee a loan.
note: Confirmed: bankrupt on 8 June 2011, debt 5.2 million, and RBC were last in the Eredivisie in 2005-06. Sub corrected: Roosendaal refused to guarantee a one million euro loan, it did not refuse a loan of its own.

q: Which Apeldoorn club went bankrupt in January 2013, two months before SC Veendam?
note: Confirmed: AGOVV declared bankrupt on 8 January 2013, SC Veendam on 25 March 2013.

q: Which club was the first Dutch professional side to play home games on artificial grass, from 2003?
sub: They took the plastic into the Eredivisie when they went up in 2005.
note: Confirmed: the first Dutch professional club on artificial grass, from a friendly against Willem II in 2003, and they took it up with them in 2005.

q: Heracles' Polman Stadion was named after what kind of business?
sub: Renamed Erve Asito in 2019 after a cleaning firm.
note: Confirmed: Polman was a real estate firm, renamed Erve Asito in 2019 after the cleaning company Asito. Moved to extreme: nobody laughs at a real estate company.

q: Which club qualified for European football for the first time in 2016 by winning the Europa League play-offs?
note: Confirmed (2-0 at Utrecht after 1-1, first Europe in 110 years). Dropped as a mirror of 'Which Almelo club finished sixth in 2015-16 and then qualified for Europe for the first time in its history?'

q: From 2006 onwards, which Ajax fixture was played without away supporters after an attack on the opponents' clubhouse?
sub: The mayor of The Hague renewed the ban season after season.
note: Confirmed: no away fans at Ajax against ADO since 2006, after Ajax fans stormed the ADO supporters' clubhouse. The old sub led on a stabbing, so it goes under the no-tragedy rule, and its 'seventy fans' figure was unverified anyway.

q: In November 2018 Feyenoord against VVV was abandoned after thirty seconds. Why?
sub: A broken transformer. The match was replayed in full on 6 December.
note: Confirmed: November 2018, stopped after about half a minute, abandoned after half an hour, a broken transformer, replayed in full on 6 December.

q: In November 2005 which Heracles goalkeeper went up for a corner and headed a stoppage-time equaliser against AZ?
sub: He was the first goalkeeper to score in the Eredivisie since 1999.
note: Header confirmed (5 November 2005, 90th minute, 2-2). Sub was embroidered twice over: the match was away at AZ, and 2005-06 was Heracles' first Eredivisie season, not their first on artificial grass, which they had laid in 2003.

q: Which Ajax substitute was sent off nineteen seconds after coming on against PSV in December 1996?
sub: He brought down Luc Nilis. Referee Dick Jol did the rest.
note: Confirmed: 22 December 1996, on for Melchiot, 19 seconds, brought down Nilis, red card from Dick Jol.

q: Edwin van der Sar scored his only career goal in May 1998, a penalty with Ajax already 7-0 up. Against whom?
sub: He had missed a penalty for Ajax against Sparta a few years earlier.
note: Goal confirmed (3 May 1998, taken at 0-7, final score 8-1). Sub trimmed: the earlier Sparta miss is real, but '8-0' and 'three years earlier' are in no source I could open.

q: Which goalkeeper scored seven Eredivisie goals between 1964 and 1967, all from the penalty spot?
note: Confirmed: seven goals for DOS and Go Ahead between 1964 and 1967, all penalties. Moved to extreme: the answer is a name nobody at the table will react to.

q: Which FC Den Bosch goalkeeper scored the Eredivisie's first goalkeeper goal from open play, in 1985?
sub: It made it 2-2 against Roda JC in the last minute, and he celebrated with a cartwheel.
note: Confirmed: 8 September 1985, the first goalkeeper to score from open play in the Eredivisie. Sub added, since the cartwheel is what makes this a ball question at all.

q: In 1975 Guus Hiddink's shot for De Graafschap went wide, a team-mate kicked the ball into the net as a joke, and what did the referee do?
sub: Sietze Veen's joke, against Haarlem. The linesman backed the referee.
note: Confirmed: De Graafschap against Haarlem in 1975, Hiddink's shot went out of play, Sietze Veen put it in as a joke and referee Louis Beukman gave the goal after consulting his linesman.

q: Where did Ajax and Feyenoord hooligans hold a pre-arranged fight in March 1997 that left one man dead?
a: A field beside the A9 motorway near Beverwijk
sub: Ajax fan Carlo Picornie died. The fight lasted about five minutes.
note: Dropped on the house rule: the question trades on a death. Carlo Picornie was killed in that fight.

q: Johan Cruyff's first Klassieker in a Feyenoord shirt, in September 1983, ended with what score?
sub: Feyenoord still won the double that season.
note: Confirmed: 18 September 1983, Ajax 8-2, the biggest score in the Klassieker and Cruyff's first against Ajax in a Feyenoord shirt. Feyenoord did win the double that season.

q: Marco van Basten's Ajax debut in April 1982 came as a substitute for which player?
sub: He scored in a 5-0 win over NEC, aged 17.
note: Debut confirmed (3 April 1982, on for Cruyff, scored). Sub rebuilt: 'Cruyff's 250th game' and 'within ten minutes' are in no source I could open, so they go.

q: The Amsterdam Arena opened in August 1996 with Ajax losing 0-3 to which club?
sub: Dejan Savićević scored the first goal in the stadium.
note: Confirmed: 14 August 1996, Ajax 0-3 AC Milan, and the first goal in the ground came from Savicevic.

q: De Kuip opened in March 1937 with a 5-2 friendly win over a club from which country?
sub: A friendly was chosen so the entrances and buffets could be tested first.
note: Confirmed in full, including the sub: 27 March 1937, 5-2 against Beerschot of Belgium, and a friendly was chosen deliberately over an international so the parking, entrances and buffets could be tested with a smaller crowd.

q: Ajax's last match at De Meer, in April 1996, ended 5-1 against which club?
sub: Finidi George scored a hat-trick. Willem II's Jack de Gier got the last goal at the ground.
note: Confirmed: 28 April 1996, 5-1 against Willem II. Sub added, both details from the same source.

q: Before the Arena, Ajax played their big European nights at which Amsterdam ground rather than De Meer?
note: Confirmed: Ajax used the Olympic Stadium for their big European and midweek games from 1930, since De Meer had no proper floodlights until the mid 1970s.

q: Ajax won the 1972 European Cup final against Inter in which Dutch stadium?
note: Confirmed: 31 May 1972, De Kuip, Ajax 2-0 Inter, both goals from Cruyff.

q: Sparta's ground is called Het Kasteel. Why?
a: A small castle-like building with two towers, left from the 1916 ground
note: Answer corrected. The castle is a separate small building with two towers, the only surviving part of the 1916 Stadion Spangen, which the Kasteel stand now backs onto. It is not the main stand facade.

q: NEC's Goffert stadium was built in the 1930s as what kind of project?
a: A work-relief scheme for the unemployed
sub: It took 202,417 working days. NEC only moved in after the war.
note: Work-relief scheme confirmed, opened 1939, NEC tenants from 1945-46. The 450,000 cubic metres was wrong: sources give 80,000. Replaced with the sourced 202,417 working days.

q: FC Groningen's Euroborg, opened in 2006, was built with which extras inside the stadium?
a: A cinema, a casino and a supermarket
note: Confirmed: the Euroborg complex holds a casino, a cinema and a supermarket, plus a school and a gym.

q: PSV's stadium stands on the company sports ground where the club was founded in 1913. What was that ground called?
note: Confirmed (Philips Sportpark, a sports field for Philips staff from 1910). Dropped: no story, and the Classic bank already asks 'Which company founded PSV?' with the answer Philips, which gives most of this away.

q: Which 19-year-old Ajax striker won the European Golden Shoe in 1982 with 32 league goals?
note: Confirmed (32 goals, aged 19, youngest winner of the award). Dropped as a near-verbatim duplicate of the shipping row 'Which Ajax striker won the 1982 European Golden Boot with 32 Eredivisie goals?'

q: Which striker won the Eredivisie golden boot five times, four with Ajax in the 1970s and once with Sparta in 1981?
note: Confirmed: four in a row with Ajax from 1974-75 and a fifth with Sparta in 1980-81. Moved to extreme, and flagging that both halves already ship separately, one as an Ajax question and one as a Sparta question.

q: Who were the first champions of Dutch professional football, in 1955?
sub: Sealed on 20 July with a 3-2 win at Eindhoven.
note: Confirmed: Willem II took the first professional title on the last day, 20 July 1955, winning 3-2 at Eindhoven while NAC lost at home to PSV.

q: Which Eindhoven club, not PSV, were Dutch champions in 1954, the last title of the amateur era?
note: Confirmed: EVV Eindhoven took the 1954 title, the last of the amateur era, beating DOS 3-1 in the decider.

q: Which club, later famous for its plastic pitch, were Dutch champions in 1927 and 1941?
note: Confirmed: champions on 19 June 1927 and again on 22 June 1941, the second sealed by beating PSV 6-1.

q: Which club won back-to-back Dutch championships in 1942 and 1943, during the occupation?
note: Confirmed: champions in 1942 and 1943, both under the occupation, with Wim Tap as coach.

q: Which Hague club had won ten Dutch championships by 1914, at a time when Ajax had none?
note: Confirmed: ten Dutch championships between 1890-91 and 1913-14, the most successful club in the country before the First World War.

q: Which Rotterdam club won the 1958-59 Eredivisie and had not won it again by 2018?
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a duplicate twice over: the shipping bank has 'Which Rotterdam club won the 1958-59 Eredivisie, and had not won another title by the end of 2006-07?', and the same question also sits in checked-history.json from the history slice.

q: Ajax won the first Eredivisie in 1957 under a coach from which country?
note: Confirmed (Karl Humenberger, Austrian). Dropped as a mirror of the shipping row 'Which Austrian coached Ajax to the first Eredivisie title in 1956-57?'

q: In 1966-67 Ajax scored how many league goals, a total no Eredivisie side had matched by 2018?
note: Confirmed (122 goals, still unmatched). Dropped because a shipping question states the number outright: 'Ajax scored 122 league goals in 1966-67. Who was top scorer that season with 33?'

q: PSV were champions on 8 April 1978, the earliest date in the league's history at the time. Which club did they beat that day?
sub: Kees Rijvers' side also won the UEFA Cup that spring.
note: The answer was wrong. PSV clinched it on 8 April with a 3-1 home win over FC Twente, then lost at Haarlem and at home to Ajax but WON their last match 1-0 at FC Utrecht, so they did not lose both of the last two. Rebuilt around the clinching game and moved to hard now that the twist is gone.

q: In 1969-70 Ajax lost 2-1 to AZ '67 in the cup and still went through to the quarter-final. How?
a: As a lucky loser, the best beaten team went through
sub: Rinus Michels called it a crazy business. Ajax went on to beat PSV 2-0 in the final.
note: Confirmed: lost 2-1 to AZ '67 in the third round on 12 April 1970, went through as lucky loser, won the cup, and the rule was scrapped straight afterwards. Sub corrected: it contradicted the very next row, since Lucky Ajax dates from 1958.

q: The phrase Lucky Ajax first appeared in De Telegraaf in 1958, copied from a nickname for which English club?
note: Confirmed: De Telegraaf used 'lucky Ajax' in September 1958 for a fortunate Van der Kuil goal against Willem II, borrowed from the Lucky Arsenal the Dutch papers were writing about.

q: Which Amsterdam merger club knocked Inter out of the 1974-75 UEFA Cup and was dissolved seven years later?
sub: Blauw-Wit plus DWS. Cologne beat them in the quarter-final.
note: Confirmed: Blauw-Wit plus DWS from 20 June 1972, beat Inter in the 1974-75 UEFA Cup, lost the quarter-final 8-3 on aggregate to 1. FC Koln, disbanded in May 1982.

q: FC Den Haag was formed in 1971 when ADO merged with which other club from The Hague?
sub: The city wanted one subsidised club. The name ADO came back in 1996.
note: Confirmed (1 July 1971, ADO plus Holland Sport). Dropped as a duplicate of 'Which Scheveningen club merged with ADO in 1971 to form FC Den Haag?', same answer.

q: Before Feyenoord, Willem van Hanegem scored 26 goals in 1967-68 for a Rotterdam merger club that folded that summer. Which?
sub: The rest of the team managed nineteen between them.
note: Dropped as a duplicate of 'Willem van Hanegem joined Feyenoord in 1968 from which Rotterdam club, which went bankrupt that same year?'. The wording was also loose: Xerxes/DHC '66 was a Rotterdam and Delft merger that played its home games in Delft. The 26 goals and the nineteen for everyone else both check out.

q: Which merger of a Schiedam club and a Dordrecht club played a single Eredivisie season, in 1991-92?
note: Premise false. SVV/Dordrecht'90 played two Eredivisie seasons under that name, 1991-92 and 1992-93, not one. It is also already shipping as 'Which merged club, formed from SVV and Dordrecht '90, finished bottom of the Eredivisie in 1992-93?'

q: FC Groningen was created in 1971 out of the professional section of which older Groningen club?
note: Confirmed: FC Groningen founded on 16 June 1971 out of GVAV. Moved to hard: a plain fact with no story.

q: AZ carried a number in their name until 1986. Which number, and why?
note: Confirmed: AZ '67 from the 1967 merger of Alkmaar '54 and FC Zaanstreek, the '67 dropped in 1986. Moved to hard.

q: Vitesse's name is the French word for what?
note: Confirmed: the founders chose Vitesse, French for speed, in May 1892. Moved to normal: no story, and the answer is a guess for anyone with school French.

q: Feyenoord take their name from what?
note: Confirmed: named after the Rotterdam district Feijenoord, adopted in 1912. Moved to normal.

q: Excelsior Rotterdam's name is a Latin word meaning what?
note: Confirmed as Latin, the comparative of excelsus. Trimmed to one answer: 'ever upward' is the motto rendering rather than the literal meaning, and the reader needs one thing to judge. Moved to normal.

q: De Graafschap was founded in 1954, the year professional football arrived. What does the name mean?
a: The county, after the old county of Zutphen in the Achterhoek
note: Confirmed: founded on 1 February 1954 for the breakaway NBVB, named after the old county of Zutphen, now the Achterhoek. Moved to hard.

q: PEC Zwolle are 'de Blauwvingers'. According to legend, how did the people of Zwolle get blue fingers?
a: Counting the copper coins Kampen paid them for their church bells
note: Confirmed as a legend, which the question is careful to say. Zwolle sold its carillon to Kampen and was paid in copper coins. Historians think the real origin is a 16th century trade quarrel, but the question asks only for the legend.

q: Excelsior's fans and players are known as the Kralingers. Why?
a: The club is based in the Kralingen district of Rotterdam
note: Confirmed: Excelsior is based in Kralingen and the nickname follows. Moved to normal: the question all but answers itself.

q: Which PSV record scorer was nicknamed Skiete Willy?
sub: Skiete is Brabant dialect for shooting. His statue stands outside the stadium.
note: Confirmed. Dropped as a duplicate of the shipping row 'Which PSV striker was nicknamed Skiete Willy for his shooting with both feet?', same answer.

q: PSV's Coen Dillen, 43 goals in 1956-57, was known by which nickname?
note: Confirmed: Coen Dillen, 43 goals in 1956-57, nicknamed Het Kanon.

q: At Barcelona, Johan Neeskens was nicknamed after the more famous team-mate he had also played with at Ajax. What was it?
note: The setting was wrong. The nickname was given to him at Barcelona, not at Ajax, and in Spanish or Catalan: Johan Segundo, or Johan Segon.

q: Which bird sits on ADO Den Haag's badge, taken from the city's coat of arms?
note: Confirmed (stork, from the city arms). Dropped as a duplicate of 'Which bird gives ADO Den Haag their nickname De Ooievaars, taken from the city's coat of arms?'

q: De Graafschap's most fanatical fans stand on a terrace named after a famous Liverpool one. What is it called?
sub: A Dutch corruption of Anfield's Spion Kop, nothing to do with spiders.
note: The spider's web was invented. The Spinnekop, built in November 1969, is named after the Spion Kop at Anfield, itself named after the Boer War hill. Question and sub rebuilt on the real origin.

q: NAC Breda's hardcore stand is known by which single letter?
note: Confirmed: NAC's best known fanatical section is the B-Side, formally Vak E, the name carried over from the old Beatrixstraat ground.

q: Sparta were relegated for the first time in their history in 2002. Which famous name was their coach?
sub: Within eighteen months he was managing Barcelona.
note: Confirmed: first relegation in the club's history in 2001-02, under Rijkaard, and Barcelona about fourteen months later. The club-site src returns 403, so it is swapped.

q: Which Dutch pop singer became chairman of FC Volendam in 2022 and was removed by the supervisory board in 2023?
sub: The board he led was dismissed as a whole in November 2023.
note: 'Within months' was wrong. Smit took office on 1 July 2022 and accepted his dismissal on 30 November 2023, roughly seventeen months. Dated properly and a sub added.

q: Which fishing town produced the Ajax brothers Gerrie and Arnold Mühren?
note: Confirmed: both brothers born in Volendam, both played for Ajax. Moved to normal: no story, and the Classic bank already pairs Volendam with the words 'fishing town'.

q: Which Ajax midfielder stood juggling the ball in the middle of a 1973 European Cup semi-final at the Bernabéu?
note: Confirmed: Gerrie Muhren, second leg of the 1972-73 European Cup semi-final at the Bernabeu, where he plucked the ball out of the air and kept it up five times. He scored the winner too.

q: What was Rinus Michels' day job when Ajax hired him in January 1965?
a: PE teacher at a school for deaf children
note: Confirmed: gym teacher at the J.C. Ammanschool for deaf children from 1956 until Ajax appointed him on 22 January 1965.

q: Which Welsh coach gave a 16-year-old Ruud Gullit his debut at Haarlem in 1979?
sub: The same man who added Eagles to Go Ahead's name.
note: Confirmed: Welsh, gave the 16-year-old Gullit his Eredivisie debut in August 1979, and Go Ahead added Eagles on his suggestion. The English Wikipedia src is a 404, so it is swapped for the Dutch page that carries both claims.

q: In March 1987 PSV sacked their coach and promoted his assistant, Guus Hiddink, who won the treble a year later. Who was sacked?
note: Confirmed (Hiddink took over on 16 March 1987, treble in 1987-88). Dropped as a duplicate of 'Whom did Guus Hiddink replace as PSV coach in March 1987, on the way to his first title?'

q: Johan Cruyff came back to Ajax in December 1981, aged 34. What did the club win in 1982 and 1983?
a: Two league titles, and the 1983 KNVB Cup as well
sub: Then they let him go, and he did the double at Feyenoord.
note: The answer was incomplete, which left two answers defensible. Ajax won the league in 1981-82 and again in 1982-83, and in 1982-83 they also won the KNVB Cup, with Cruyff scoring his last Ajax goal in the final.
